newsitem.title: CHINA: China to regulate chaotic insurance market.
newsitem.headline: China to regulate chaotic insurance market.

text.p: China will take tough measures to regulate its insurance market to curb increasing irregularities, the China Securities daily said on Wednesday.
The central bank, the market regulator, would start from this month to check insurance companies across the country and try to bring order to the market, the newspaper said.
China recently held a meeting on supervision of the insurance market to curb financial risk, it said.
Dai Xianglong, the central bank governor has said falling inflation would enable the bank to focus on reform of financial controls, reduce unhealthy assets and improve risk management.
The reform of China's insurance system has lagged behind the improvement of the financial sector as a whole, the paper said.
Lack of regulations had fuelled increasing irregularities in the market, including the setting up of unauthorised insurance outlets, random commission collection and illegal payments.
The central bank would close insurance outlets set up without official approval, scrap illegal insurance clauses and check commission charges, premium rates and payments, it said.
Officials responsible for processing fake policies and accounts would be severely punished, the newspaper said.
